figures.finding: France taxes a household's income by a progressive scale on each share (quotient familial); the scale set by the loi de finances pour 2026 for 2025 income is 0% to €11,600, then 11%, 30%, 41% and 45% above €181,917. The scale for 2026 income awaits the loi de finances pour 2027.
figures.applies: Resident households; national tax only (no regional or municipal income tax layer). The 2025-income scale is what is assessed in 2026; the 2026-income scale is a blocker.

figures.finding: On a salary the employee pays 6.9% capped old-age (to the €4,005 monthly ceiling) and 0.4% uncapped, plus CSG 9.2% and CRDS 0.5% on 98.25% of gross; the employer pays 13% (or 7%) health, 8.55% capped and 2.11% uncapped old-age, 5.25% (or 3.45%) family and 4% unemployment, with Agirc-Arrco top-ups on both sides. An artiste-auteur pays 6.90% capped old-age (6.15% after the State's share), CSG 9.20%, CRDS 0.50% and 0.35% training on income up to the €48,060 annual ceiling.

figures.finding: Sums paid for artistic performances given or used in France to a performer with no professional base there, salaries included, bear a 15% withholding on the gross less a flat 10% for expenses; it is final up to the article 182 A limit and the excess is taxed on the progressive scale with credit for the tax withheld (75% for non-salary sums to a non-cooperative state).

sources.said: La retenue à la source prévue par l' article 182 A bis du CGI est liquidée au taux de 15 %.

La base de la retenue à la source est constituée par le montant brut des rémunérations versées, y compris les salaires, après déduction d'un abattement forfaitaire de 10 % au titre des frais professionnels.
la retenue à la source prélevée au taux de 15 % est libératoire de l'impôt sur le revenu pour la fraction de rémunération n'excédant pas la limite d'application
Le VI de l’ article 182 A bis du CGI porte à 75 % le taux de la retenue à la source applicable

figures.finding: Authors' royalties declared in full by the payer are taxed under the rules for salaries (with the standard 10% deduction), unless the author opts for non-commercial profits (BNC); either way the author may spread exceptional income by averaging under article 100 bis.

value.averaging: CGI art. 100 bis, combinable with 1 quater

figures.finding: A freelancer is exempt from VAT (franchise en base) while turnover stays within €37,500 for services (€41,250 in the current year); for authors and performers, deliveries of works and assignments of rights have their own thresholds of €50,000 (€55,000), and their other activities €35,000 (€38,500). Once liable, an author's assignment of rights bears 10% and other operations 20%; a publisher, collecting society or producer that is itself registered withholds the VAT on authors' rights (net 9.20% in metropolitan France).
